definition.description: From a bilateral standing base over a marked, clear floor target, hold an intact impact-rated medicine ball or slam ball with both hands, load through the hips and legs, extend to take the ball overhead, brace, and release it straight down into the target. Complete the declared dead-ball retrieval or controlled catch before resetting. One repetition is not a scoop slam, a rotational side slam, a throw to a wall or partner, a rebound-to-catch task, or a tall-kneeling slam.

environment.space: one athlete at a time in a protected floor-impact and retrieval zone with no bystanders or cross traffic
inspection: verify the ball is intact and appropriate for repeated floor impact
verify floor target, floor surface, overhead clearance, and retrieval path
keep other people out of the impact and rebound zone
confirm grip, footwear, communication, and controlled stop path

understands the target, reset, and stop signal

pain, loss of grip, dizziness, neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or communication concern

provenance.identityAuthority: Source 152 plus ball-slam-foundations-v1 packet. Sources 1161 and 1167 remain separately archived duplicate lineage; implement construction and split stance are controlled variants, while kneeling and rotational slams are distinct definitions.

anatomy.claimsBoundary: Task mechanics and likely loading sites only; no diagnosis, treatment, injury-prevention, isolated activation, or guaranteed performance claim.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate standing overhead-to-floor ballistic throw exposure when the exact ball, target, retrieval, timing, and session budgets fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Load through the hips, get tall with the ball, brace, then throw straight through the floor target and reset safely.
secondaryCues: use a ball that stays fast and controllable
keep the target directly below the release path
catch only when that rule is assigned
end the set before it becomes a slow arm-only effort
expectedSensations: whole-body leg, trunk, shoulder, and grip effort
brief high-intent ballistic effort followed by a deliberate reset
unexpectedSensations: back, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, knee, or foot pain
loss of grip, unsafe rebound, dizziness, or loss of balance
selfChecks: ball is intact and the zone is clear
release remains straight into the marked target
trunk stays organized without a backward lean or uncontrolled fold
the assigned catch or retrieval is controlled

observationChecklist: exact standing bilateral overhead-to-floor identity, not scoop, rotation, wall throw, kneeling, or reactive rebound catch
ball construction/mass, floor target, ceiling, spacing, rebound and retrieval route
hip and leg load, overhead path, trunk organization, target accuracy, grip, catch/retrieval, speed loss, symptoms, and first quality loss

faultCorrections.arm_only_or_slow_slam: reduce ball mass or repetitions, restore hip-and-leg load and overhead path, then end the set if speed does not return
faultCorrections.backward_lean_or_lumbar_dominance: reduce load and range of counter-movement, restore rib-pelvis organization, or stop
faultCorrections.target_drift_or_unsafe_rebound: reset the marked zone and dead-ball retrieval rule; do not count or continue uncontrolled releases

doNotUseWhen: a rotational, scoop-start, tall-kneeling, wall/partner throw, or rebound-catch objective is intended
the ball, floor, overhead clearance, target, rebound/retrieval path, or communication is unsafe
the exact task conflicts with symptoms, restrictions, or current ballistic-throw/fatigue budget
